Hi Avery,

Thanks for taking the time with us last week. As discussed, we9re evaluating a reserved GPU pool at Redwood for q3 production and I9m sending a small sample of our traffic and a draft MSA for early review (see attachments). A few quick context points: 
- Primary workload: conversational search + long-form summarization (avg context ~2,200 tokens, peaks to ~6,000).
- Peak qps: 160 requests/sec during sync windows; typical steady state ~55 req/s.
- Concurrency per model instance: bursts up to 420 concurrent inflight inference contexts during batch windows.

Questions for your pricing and packaging team:
1) What committed pool size would you recommend for this mix (we want a predictable monthly bill + throughput SLA)?
2) How do discount tiers shift for 12 vs 36 month commits?
3) Are there recommended burst/credit policies for our usage shape?

We9d like a short written sizing recommendation so our procurement team can get a rough budget. Procurement contact is procurement@procurecorp.com.

Thanks,
Samantha Park
Head of Platform
Deckarm Inc

Samantha — thanks for the data and the MSA. I pulled a quick pass through the sample and looped in Marcus (solutions) to validate our throughput assumptions. A few clarifying asks before Marcus and I produce a scenario doc: 
- Can you confirm average request size in tokens (you listed avg context ~2,200 but we9d like avg request tokens separate from context length)?
- Are the 160 qps observed at a single region or cross-region traffic?
- How tolerant is the app to 100-300ms tail latency vs <100ms? That changes batching and recommended node types.

High level we9re thinking in two scenarios:
A) Performance-first (latency SLO <120ms p95): smaller number of high-memory A100S-equivalent nodes with conservative batching.
B) Cost-first (latency up to 250ms p95 acceptable): larger pool with more aggressive batching and prefix caching.

If you9re available I can schedule a 30-min sizing call tomorrow; Marcus will bring a worksheet with detailed token/QPS-to-GPU mappings. I9ll also flag pricing with Karthik for a 12 vs 36-month discount matrix.

—Avery
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Avery —

Answers below inline: 
- Avg request tokens (input + LLM prompt) ~820 tokens; avg response ~480 tokens. Context window is additional history we append (~1,100 tokens).
- Traffic is single-region (us-west) for now; cross-region planned in 2028.
- Latency tolerance: for customer-facing search we9d like p95 <180ms; for backend summarization p95 can be up to 300ms.

Procurement asked for two named scenarios (they want a best-guess so they can route budget):
1) Pilot 3-month commit (start small, commit to scale month 3) — target initial spend ~ $50k/mo.
2) Annual commit (12 months) — want to understand discount tiers and if there9s an escalation clause for growth.

If Marcus has a mapping doc we9d appreciate a clear recommended GPU pool with conversion to monthly committed dollars so procurement can triage.

Samantha

Samantha / Avery — looping in pricing and legal. Marcus attached an updated workbook (Dedicated_Sizing_Workbook.xlsx) to this thread and I9ve sketched two committed scenarios below based on the tokens/qps you provided and our internal perf profiles: 

Scenario 1 — Pilot / Short term ramp (3-month window)- Recommended committed pool: 8 vGPU-equivalent slots (approximately equivalent to 4 x A100S 80GB nodes in our packing)- Throughput target: steady 55 req/s, burst capacity to 160 req/s using burst credits + autoscale to reserved headroom- Expected monthly committed spend: ~$48k/mo- Discount: pilot pricing uses limited 10% onboarding credit applied month 1; standard 5% volume discount for 3-month commit

Scenario 2 — Annual commit (12 months)- Recommended committed pool: 12 vGPU-equivalent slots (approximately 6 x A100S 80GB nodes) to hit p95 <180ms for search and preserve headroom for summarization- Throughput target: baseline 70 req/s, sustained bursts to 160 req/s via reserved capacity + burst buffer- Expected monthly committed spend: ~$36k/mo (net of 18% commitment discount)- Additional perks: 2 free months of extended observability retention and a guaranteed burst credit pool that replenishes monthly

Notes and assumptions:
- We assume prefix/KV caching will reduce token work for repeated prompts by ~12-20%; if your cache hit rate is higher we can reduce recommended committed slots.
- Context length peaks to 6,000 tokens will increase memory pressure; we9ve sized for an 80GB-class node equivalent to avoid OOMs in long-history requests.
- SLA: 99.9% uptime for Dedicated with route fallback to our hosted API (for soft degradation) — we can discuss higher SLA and associated uplift.

Next steps suggested:
1) Marcus to share the workbook mapping token counts -> vGPU slots (attached).
2) Procurement to confirm which scenario (Pilot vs Annual) they prefer and share PO lead.
3) Monica to review MSA redline and return high-level legal notes within 3 business days.

Happy to jump on a call to walk through the workbook live.

—Karthik Iyer
Director, Pricing & Packaging, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Dedicated_Sizing_Workbook.xlsx
